agent_notes: Corrected the heading's position as asked: Pss 120–134 are fifteen Songs of the Ascents and 132 is the thirteenth. The title is counted as part of Hebrew verse 1 (KJV 132:0 and 132:1).

STEPBible glosses עֻנּוֹתוֹ as 'being afflicted he'; I glossed it 'his afflictions', a noun with a possessive suffix. Ibn Ezra on this verse calls it a noun from the same root as עִנּוּי. The Targum's 'סִגוּפֵיהּ' (his mortifications) agrees with the noun reading.

agent_notes: STEPBible glosses בַּעֲבוּר as 'forsake of', which is wrong (a slip from the root עזב). Corrected to 'for the sake of'. In the verse the hiphil of שׁוב with פנים is 'turn back the face', i.e. refuse a petitioner; BBE's 'give up your king' is an interpretation. Whether 'anointed' is David or his successor is open (Rashi on Psalms 132:10 says Solomon, Ibn Ezra says David); the text does not name him.

Rewrote the echo as asked. In v. 10 God is asked not to turn back (hiphil תָּשֵׁב) the anointed's face; in v. 11 God himself will not turn back (qal יָשׁוּב) from the oath. Same root שוב, God the subject both times.

agent_notes: Qere-style oddities: עֵדֹתִי is pointed with holem (Ibn Ezra, Radak, Meiri note it stands for the shureq form עֵדוּתִי / 'testimony'), and אֲלַמְּדֵם is imperfect ('I will teach them'), which Meiri and Ibn Ezra discuss. The relative זוֹ is a rare feminine form; Rashi glosses it 'that which I shall teach them'. I read it as 'my testimonies, which I will teach them'. 'Their sons also' (גם־בניהם) starts the apodosis with the verb יֵשְׁבוּ at the end of the verse.

history.note: [consider] Either render 'my testimony' to follow the commentators and the singular זוֹ, or say in the note why you keep the plural. (PS.132.12: "וְעֵדֹתִי זוֹ אֲלַמְּדֵם"; Radak: "ועדותי. בחולם כמו בשורק".)

agent_notes: Revised per the reviewer's request: the earlier claim that the KJV drops a preposition, and the reading that the choice happened 'inside' Zion, are removed. בָּחַר regularly takes its object with בְּ (as in 'chose Zion'), so token 4 is glossed 'Zion' with the preposition marked as the verb's object marker, and the literal layer reads 'has chosen Zion'.

The five English versions agree on the sense and differ only in register: YLT 'fixed on' and BBE 'heart is on' render the verb's choosing idiomatically. The Metzudat Zion citation (Job 23:13) is as given in the packet. The Radak and Malbim claims are summarised from the packet text only.

In the literal layer write 'has chosen Zion' (or 'has chosen [in] Zion'), and gloss token 4 'Zion' or '<in> Zion'. (PS.132.13: "כִּי־בָחַר יְהוָה בְּצִיּוֹן"; STEPBible puts the preposition in angle brackets, '<in> Zion', marking it as the object marker of the verb, not a translatable 'in'.)

agent_notes: Verse 14 switches from the narrator (v. 13, 'the LORD has chosen') to YHWH speaking in the first person. The Hebrew has no quotation marker; I added none in the literal layer and let the dramatic layer carry the shift. Malbim reads it as God's answer to 'Arise, O LORD, to your resting place' (v. 8).

צֵידָהּ is vocalized with mappiq in the he (so 'her', a suffix), and the lemma is צַיִד 'game, provisions'. Ketiv/Qere is not at issue, but the word is rare: Radak and Meiri take it as 'provision' (as in 'provision for the road'). The KJV 'abundantly bless' renders the infinitive absolute בָּרֵךְ אֲבָרֵךְ; the literal layer keeps the doubling. Radak's note on the mappiq (relating the word to a different noun) is cryptic in the packet and I did not rely on it.

agent_notes: I glossed מְשִׁיחִי as 'my anointed one' (the king), not as a capitalized title. The messianic readings of Radak and Meiri are quoted only as commentary; the Hebrew itself names the Davidic king.

history.note: [consider] Drop the claim about the KJV and 'my anointed'; consider dropping 'and it will not go out' from the dramatic layer. (PS.132.17 KJV: "I have ordained a lamp for mine anointed".)

agent_notes: STEPBible lists נִזְרוֹ under the lemma נָסָה (H5145H), which looks like a lemma error; the word is נֵזֶר 'consecrated diadem' (root נזר). I glossed it 'his crown/diadem'. The verb יָצִיץ 'will blossom/shine' (root צוץ) is the point of the verse: the same verb family as the high priest's gold ציץ (Exod 28:36), which Radak mentions.

אביר יעקב is a title of God (Gen 49:24, Isa 49:26): 'the Mighty One of Jacob'. KJV adds 'God' without italics here. Note also that the two verbs of the verse, 'swore' and 'vowed', are a poetic pair (Radak: the matter doubled in other words).

agent_notes: Dropped the locative claim: בְאֶפְרָתָה is the name Ephrathah with the preposition בְּ 'in', as the reviewer said. The ark reading of the feminine suffix is a modern one and is marked as such in the commentary. Rashi and Metzudat David do not read it that way, and Radak takes the feminine to mean the Divine Presence.

The five English versions agree on 'wood/forest' for יָעַר. I kept 'Jaar' in the literal layer because the Hebrew has no article and the packet's registry ties it to Kiriath-jearim; that identification is the modern one, not the packet commentators', who point to Ornan's threshing floor.

agent_notes: עֻנּוֹתוֹ: в Синодальном «кротости его» (Пс 131:1); в литеральном слое — «его смирения/самоистязания» через «страдания», в драматическом — «всё, что он вытерпел». В комментарии объяснено, что комментаторы читают слово как добровольное самоограничение Давида.

agent_notes: פְּרִי בִטְנְךָ: сохранено «плод чрева твоего», как в Синодальном.

В синодальном переводе этот псалом — 131-й, а эти стихи — 12–17; нумерация здесь по еврейскому тексту. «Жилище» (мошав) совпадает с синодальным; Сион в драматическом слое — мужского рода русского слова («по нему»), хотя в иврите суффикс женский.
«меная» исправлено на «менуха» (транслитерация מְנוּחָה, как в английском m'nuchah).

agent_notes: Название יָעַר: в Синодальном «поля Иаарские», Ефрафа — «Ефрафа»; прежнее соглашение корпуса для Ефраты/Эфрафы ещё не задано, выбрана синодальная форма «Ефрафа». Местоимение женского рода оставлено без антецедента: в Синодальном «о нём» (мужской род), здесь «о ней».
חֲסִידֶיךָ: Синодальный «преподобные», но комментарий (как и английский, критикующий «saints») объясняет «верные завету»; в переводных слоях выбрано «верные Твои».
